Direct per-haul submissions to ICES DATRAS: HH (haul), HL (length), CA (age), LT (litter), as they actually exist in the published archive. The IMBUS/archive-side dictionary: curated from ICES's own sources and verified against real submissions (enum values restricted to archive-observed codes; physical non-negativity bounds expressed as assertions). Keyed by opus's current field names; each column's details carries the legacy on-the-wire name. See data-raw/spec/spec_02_curate_dict.R for the corrections and field-spec fills applied and why. For ICES's own documented view of the same format, see inst/DATRAS-ices.yaml.

::: {.callout-note}
Generated from `inst/DATRAS-imbus.yaml` by `data-raw/DATASET_dict_to_qmd.R`. Edit the YAML and regenerate -- don't hand-edit this file.
:::

## HH

*Haul Information*
Each row is one haul (trawl deployment). Contains haul-level metadata: geography, timing, gear deployment, environmental conditions, and performance flags.
Grain: each row represents one discrete haul deployment (one trawl operation). Population: all hauls submitted to ICES DATRAS within the covered survey/region/timeframe. Join key: HL, CA, and LT tables reference haul-level data via a composite identifier constructed from eight fields: Survey, Year, Quarter, Country, {Platform or Ship}, Gear, {StationName or StNo}, and HaulNumber. The naming convention differs by era: newer submissions use Platform/StationName/HaulNumber (new style); older submissions use Ship/StNo/HaulNo (old style). Note: HaulNumber alone is NOT a valid join key and must be paired with all seven other fields -- but even the full composite key doesn't recover everything: 305,276 CA rows (5.12% of 5,968,027) carry no haul number and match no HH haul on any subset of the 8 fields. As submitted these are a -9 sentinel; in the published archive HaulNumber is sentinel policy 'strip', so they arrive as null. They are real observations attributed to an area rather than a haul -- 305,146 carry an Age and together they hold 599,407 aged fish -- and must be accounted for at area grain, not dropped to make a join succeed. See DATRAS-known-issues.yaml (ca_haulno_unlinkable_to_hh) and CA's own `linkable_to_hh` definition.

Unlike HaulNo's own -9 sentinel, this isn't an orphaning problem: CA's own matching StNo=-9 rows for these same hauls (191,893 rows) join HH successfully via the other 7 composite-key fields, since both sides consistently carry -9 for the same haul rather than disagreeing. |

## HL

*Length Frequency Distribution*
Each row is a length class within a haul's catch. Contains the count of fish in each length bin, without individual-level age/sex data; the length-aggregated summary layer of Tier 1.
Grain: each row is a (haul, species, length class) combination with a count of fish in that length bin. Population: length-frequency summaries for all species caught in surveyed hauls, aggregated by length class. Linked to HH via the composite haul identifier (Survey + Year + Quarter + Country + Platform/Ship + Gear + StationName/StNo + HaulNumber). Note: CA (not HL) has a verified HaulNumber/HaulNo linkage gap -- 5.12% of CA rows carry no haul number (a -9 sentinel as submitted, null in the published archive) and match no HH haul even via the full composite key (see HH table details). The full 8-field composite key is required for correct joins regardless.

## CA

*Age Composition (Individual)*
Each row is one aged fish specimen from a haul. Contains individual-level biological measurements (length, weight, age, sex, maturity) on a subsample of the catch; linked to HH via the composite haul identifier.
Grain: each row is one biological specimen (a single aged fish) from a haul. Population: individual organisms sampled and measured from hauls within covered surveys, not the full catch — a subsample. Linked to HH via the composite haul identifier (Survey + Year + Quarter + Country + Platform/Ship + Gear + StationName/StNo + HaulNumber). Note (see DATRAS-known-issues.yaml issue ca_haulno_unlinkable_to_hh): as submitted, HaulNumber/HaulNo contains 0 true nulls -- 305,276 rows (5.12% of 5,968,027) instead carry a -9 sentinel, which violates the column's declared range ([0, 82483]; a D04_range violation, confirmed via op_flag_violations()), not the required constraint (D01 never fires here). These rows match no HH haul on the full 8-field composite key, or on the 7 non-HaulNumber fields alone -- not a join-key problem, but genuinely orphaned CA records. A separate, much smaller residual (700 rows, 0.01%) with a plausible HaulNumber also fails to match HH.

## LT

*Litter Assessment*
Each row is one litter observation from a haul. Contains types and counts of marine debris (plastics, fishing gear, natural/organic material) recorded during the catch review; a separate thematic addition to the HH/HL/CA exchange.
Grain: each row is one litter assessment/observation recorded during a haul's catch review. Population: litter records from hauls in covered surveys; a thematic addition to the HH/HL/CA core exchange tables with a separate collection protocol and scope. Linked to HH via the composite haul identifier (Survey + Year + Quarter + Country + Platform/Ship + Gear + StationName/StNo + HaulNumber). Note: CA has a verified HaulNumber/HaulNo linkage gap via a -9 sentinel (see CA table details); LT's own HaulNumber has no equivalent gap -- zero nulls and zero -9 values. The full 8-field composite key is required for correct joins regardless: 852 of 79,451 LT rows (1.07%) don't match any HH haul on it (down from 2,026 of 75,310 when first measured -- ICES has since supplied part of the missing HH submission), but for an unrelated, diagnosed reason (known-issues.yaml: lt_bts_2025_q1_orphaned) -- HH's own submission is genuinely missing for that survey/year/quarter, not an LT-side data-quality problem.

Upper bound set at 2 hours: DATRAS carries no passive/soak gear, so a longer tow is highly suspect -- observed values run as high as 1470 min with no repeating marker pattern (i.e. not a clean sentinel, just unreliable). |

See known issue dateofcalculation_type_mismatch (DATRAS-known-issues.yaml, not yet filed): ICES's WSDL declares this field character for LT's own retrieval operation (getLitterAssessmentOutput), while HH/HL/CA's own operations all declare it int/decimal -- but real LT data is the identical 8-digit YYYYMMDD stamp (e.g. "20260625"), just returned as a string by that one operation. Digit order (month before day) is consistent with HH/HL/CA. Same open-upper-bound, ICES-Datacenter-inserted basis as HH/HL/CA's DateofCalculation, but this table's OWN verified minimum (2015-11-27) is genuinely years later than theirs (2012-04-19) -- consistent with LT/litter reporting being a newer addition to DATRAS than the main haul/length/age exchange. |
